A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ProsQA experiments, accuracy comparisons, and attention and representation analyses in Section 5, plus a three-seed stability analysis in Appendix C.2.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix C.2, including the accuracy comparisons and three-seed representation analysis.

M1.justification: The transformer construction, attention choosers, superposition updates, readout, and multistage training are unchanged. The COCONUT-BFS supervision variant in Section 5.4 already appears in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ProsQA subset with 3–4-hop graph-reachability questions (Section 5.1; Appendix C.1). No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 4 retains CoT, CoT* (12 layers and 12 heads), and No CoT as comparators to COCONUT. Section 5.4 retains the same COCONUT-BFS comparison.

E3.justification: Model configurations, optimizer settings, training schedules, evaluation procedures, and metrics remain unchanged. Table 4 retains 14,785 training, 257 validation, and 419 test problems.

E4.justification: The attention and latent-representation analyses in Section 5.3, alternative-supervision analysis in Section 5.4, and representation-stability analysis in Appendix C.2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report test-set attention means and standard deviations in Table 1 and results from three runs with different random seeds in Appendix C.2/Table 5. Reporting practices and run counts are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 4–6 and Tables 1 and 5 retain identical results. Both versions report near-perfect COCONUT and COCONUT-BFS accuracy, approximately 75% for CoT/No CoT, and 83% for the larger CoT model, with unchanged attention and representation findings.

T1.justification: The definitions, Lemmas 1–6, Theorem 1, Propositions B.1–B.4, and their proofs are unchanged, including the sinusoidal and rotary positional-encoding constructions in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same D-step graph-reachability claim, comparison with the best-known O(n²) discrete-CoT construction, and claim that superpositional search emerges through training.

C2.justification: Interpretations of buffer spaces, nonuniform node weights, and exploration priority remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same open questions about discrete-CoT lower bounds, training dynamics, and generalization to broader settings.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address in the abstract, absent from v1. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, dataset statistics, and computing-resource information in Section 5.1 and Appendix C are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 1.1 are unchanged. Bibliography entries merely reflow after the added acknowledgements.

P1.justification: v2 adds the abstract's code-access sentence and an Acknowledgements section, inserts the grammatical 'that' in Section 5.3, and updates the version/date stamp. The remaining wording and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence and acknowledgements cause limited changes to text flow and reference-page layout. Figures 1–7, Tables 1–5, and all appendix layouts remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides an explicit implementation location through its new repository address and discloses funding through acknowledgements. These offer modest gains in reproducibility documentation and transparency; the scientific claims, proofs, experimental evidence, and appendices remain unchanged.
